ledger.note: 1806: the principality continues as a state of the Holy Roman Empire's successors. 'After the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806 it was a constituent state of its successors'; the county had been raised to a principality on 6 January 1712. The German page adds that it joined the Confederation of the Rhine ('Akzessionsvertrag Waldecks zum Rheinbund, 18. April 1807') and the German Confederation in 1815. The region is the three districts named on the German page, drawn as radii.

ledger.note: September 1812: Pyrmont is reunited. The territories 'were reunited after Frederick's death', which the ruler table dates to 24 September 1812; the page gives no day for the reunion.

ledger.note: 13 November 1918: the monarchy is abolished. The ruler table gives Friedrich's reign as '12 May 1893 - 13 November 1918' and the page says the state 'declared that the monarchy was abolished' (infobox 'German Revolution: 1918'). In 1871 'the principality became a constituent state of the new German Empire'. The state itself lasted to 'on 1 April 1929, the state was abolished and became part of the Prussian' province; this dossier ends with the monarchy, like the other members, and weimar-republic carries the land. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Waldeck 'fought on the Prussian side in the Austro-Prussian War of 1866 and thus avoided annexation'; no territory changed.
wars.note: The war article was not opened (page budget). Waldeck had concluded a military convention with Prussia on 1 August 1862 (the page).

certainty.note: A small state with administrative boundaries (three districts from 1849-1850 plus Pyrmont); the pages give no survey, the Pyrmont district lay apart, and the grid cannot draw the Prussian exclaves of Höringhausen and Eimelrod. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA'S SHAPES ARE MISPLACED. All six shapes sit about 27 km west of the real Waldeck (centroid 8.63E 51.40N against Arolsen 9.01E 51.38N) and omit Pyrmont; the corrected regions are radii around Arolsen, Korbach and Wildungen (the districts named on the German page) and around Pyrmont, as the gazetteer lacks those place names. GAZETTEER NAMES WANTED: Arolsen (Bad Arolsen) 9.01E 51.38N, Korbach 8.87E 51.27N, Wildungen (Bad Wildungen) 9.12E 51.12N, Pyrmont (Bad Pyrmont) 9.26E 51.98N.

PYRMONT 1806-1812: separate principality, per the English page; the German page says only a short partition among brothers in 1806 and that Pyrmont 'since 1807 was a principality'. The reunion month rests on the ruler table (24 September 1812).

END YEAR 1871 follows the sibling German-state dossiers; the state lasted to 1 April 1929 (Prussian province of Hesse-Nassau), with Pyrmont separated on 30 November 1921.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Memberships are not ledger events: Confederation of the Rhine (1807, 'but not the Napoleonic Kingdom of Westphalia'), German Confederation (1815, 'confirmed ... by the Congress of Vienna'), Zollverein (1832), North German Confederation (after 1867). (2) The legal unification of Waldeck and Pyrmont in 1849 is a constitutional act, not a border change. (3) Area: 1,121 km2 (1905) is the only figure. (4) The principality's rulers before 1806 are in county-of-waldeck. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (principality-of-waldeck-and-pyrmont_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row principality-of-waldeck-and-pyrmont -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. Waldeck lasted as a Land of the Weimar Republic until 1 April 1929 (it has no dossier for 1918-1929); this dossier ends with the monarchy in November 1918 as the other members do.
